To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
L-Arg protects against post-eccentric exercise muscle damage, preserves exercise performance capacity, and reduces the expression of the proteolytic enzyme µ-calpain.
L-arginin supplementation prior to a bout of eccentric exercise protects against exercise induced damage of muscle fibers and improves exercise performance.
L-Arg supplementation protects against post-exercise muscle damage, and improves subsequent exercise performance capacity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of L-arginine in the prevention of muscle damage induced by eccentric exercise.
the role of native nitric oxide production in the development of muscle damage.
the role of nitric oxide (NO) in the development of muscle fiber damage and exercise performance capacity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
L-Arg, a precursor of NO, may be used to prevent exercise induced muscle damage and to improve subsequent exercise performance capacity.
L-Arg protects skeletal muscle from exercise-induced injury.
L-Arg protects exercise performance and structural integrity of muscle fibers after a single bout of exercise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
L-Arg protects muscle fibers against eccentric exercise-induced damage and preserves exercise capacity.
L-Arg protects muscle from exercise-induced damage through a mechanism that involves NOS.
L-Arg protects muscle fibers and improves exercise performance by inhibiting calpain activation and subsequent damage to muscle fibers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NOS system plays an important role in exercise performance capacity and protection from eccentric exercise-induced muscle damage.
L-Arg can be used as an effective supplement for protection of skeletal muscle against damage induced by a single bout of strenuous exercise.
L-Arg may be a promising supplement to protect muscle integrity against exercise-induced muscle damage and to preserve exercise performance capacity.
